title: ESSAY 4: Priority Sector Lending — Is Regulation the Best Tool for Inclusive Growth?

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Priority Sector Lending (PSL) mandates banks to direct a specified portion of credit towards key vulnerable sectors including agriculture, MSMEs, education, housing, and social infrastructure.

Domestic commercial banks and foreign banks with 20 or more branches must allocate at least 40% of Adjusted Net Bank Credit (ANBC) or Credit Equivalent Amount of Off-Balance Sheet Exposure (CEOBE) to priority sectors.
Regional Rural Banks (RRBs) and Small Finance Banks (SFBs) carry a higher mandatory requirement of 75% total PSL allocation.

Bank shortfalls in PSL targets are funneled into lower-yielding development funds like the Rural Infrastructure Development Fund (RIDF) managed by NABARD or adjusted using Priority Sector Lending Certificates (PSLCs).

blocks.content: Priority sector lending must evolve from a regulatory compliance burden into a viable business model for long-term inclusive growth.

rows: Balanced credit growth across key national economic sectors
Flexible credit allocation across priority categories
High-density financial inclusion for unserved and underserved segments
Dedicated credit delivery to the rural agrarian economy

items: Distinguish between standard PSL target (40% for Commercial Banks) and targeted inclusion models (75% for RRBs and SFBs).
Memorize exact sub-targets: Agriculture (18%), Micro-enterprises (7.5%), and Weaker Sections (12%).
Note the short-fall penalty funds: RIDF (NABARD), SIDBI, MUDRA, and NHB.
